meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-08 | Start: 16:00 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Karen Ito (NimbleX VP Eng), Derek Shaw (NimbleX SRE), Priya Menon (NimbleX ML)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning. Reviewed last 48h run: bursty tails, p99 spikes during concurrent bursts. Decided to try a targeted continuous batching profile plus lowered concurrency cap for latency-sensitive routes. Action items assigned for 24h steady-state run and config changes. Next call scheduled after steady-state results come in.
topics: 48h run results; continuous batching adjustments; concurrency targets per route; queue shaping/backpressure; KV prefix cache behavior; cost vs latency tradeoffs; security/KMS question; next bench run
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then Luis will walk through the telemetry from the two-day run.
[00:14] Karen: Yep, all good here. Just to flag, Derek's on for infra questions.
[00:19] Luis (SE): Okay, so summary upfront — the 48 hour run on the pilot cluster shows steady token throughput at base load but we saw a couple of, like, sharp p99 latency spikes during concurrent bursts. GPU util averaged ~72% but spiked to 98% during the 10s bursts.
[00:34] Priya: When you say bursts, is that the RPS spike or larger payloads?
[00:38] Luis: Mostly RPS, small payloads. The payload size distribution didn't change much; it's the concurrency peaks that pushed KV cache warm-up and caused a mini-thrashing effect.
[00:49] Derek: We noticed some queue growth in our ingress side too, the front-end buffer fills then the requests queue up — so there's a little backpressure that cascades.
[00:58] Maya: Right. Two levers we discussed last week: continuous batching profile and per-route concurrency caps. We tried default_batching and conservative continuous batching. The conservative batch reduced p99 but hurt throughput.
[01:12] Luis: Exactly, so the idea now is target an "aggressive continuous_batching" profile for non-latency-critical routes and lower concurrency cap (from 48 to 16) for the chat route. That should smooth the GPU utilization and avoid those 98% microspikes.
[01:27] Karen: How do you quantify latency impact — like, what does user-facing mean here? We have a few premium routes that need < 300ms p95.
[01:33] Luis: We're seeing p95 for that route around 180–220ms at steady-state with current conservative batching. If we push aggressive batching for that route, p95 may climb over 300ms. So the trade is route level: keep conservative batching for premium routes, aggressive elsewhere.
[01:46] Priya: Can we do mixed mode? Per-route flags?
[01:49] Maya: Yes, Redwood runtime supports route-level batching policies. Luis can scope the changes.
[01:53] Derek: There's also the KV cache warm-up — during burst windows your hit-rate drops to maybe 60% from 92%. That explains a lot of increase in token compute.
[02:02] Luis: Yeah, we saw the prefix cache had a knee when concurrency jumped. We're proposing to increase pre-warm threads and bump prefix cache TTL for the pilot so warm-ups are faster.
[02:11] Karen: Any concerns about memory on the nodes if TTL increases?
[02:14] Luis: Minimal, the entries are small. Current nodes have headroom. We'll monitor.
[02:18] Maya: Cost note — aggressive batching lowers tokens/sec bill but if it increases p95 on premium paths it could impact UX. We'll model cost delta in the revised pricing sheet.
[02:26] Priya: About the concurrency cap change — does that translate to more nodes? I want to understand cap 16 vs 48 in terms of capacity planning.
[02:33] Luis: Practically, lower concurrency cap means more parallel inference instances to maintain overall throughput. For the pilot, we can keep node count the same and accept slightly lower headroom, or spin up one extra nodepool for high-throughput non-premium routes. We'll test both.
[02:47] Derek: On the ingress queuing, we can shape traffic a bit upstream; our API gateway can do soft throttles too.
[02:52] Maya: Good — that's part of the playbook. 
[02:55] Karen: About security — Derek, we had a question from legal about KMS for logs and whether Redwood keeps full text.
[03:03] Derek (NimbleX): We need assurance on encryption-at-rest and key controls.
[03:07] Maya: We will share the SOC2 and KMS integration doc. Pilot logs can be configured to redacted mode; full text can be turned on only with customer-managed KMS. I'll follow up with that doc.
[03:17] Priya: Back to performance — do you have microbenchmarks for the quantized variant? We tried q4f16 on a branch model and it improved latency but changed some outputs.
[03:27] Luis: We did a small microbench. Quantization reduces per-token compute by ~18% but there were minor output regressions on the prompt set. For this pilot we'll keep the unquantized branch for premium routes, and we can A/B the quantized model for low-stakes routes.
[03:40] Karen: Sounds reasonable.
[03:42] Luis: For today's ops, plan: one nodepool will run aggressive continuous_batching with prefix TTL bumped; route concurrency cap for chat set to 16; non-chat burst routes get aggressive batching. We'll collect 24h steady-state and compare token/sec, p95/p99, GPU util and prefix cache hit-rate.
[03:58] Priya: Can you log the KV cache hit-rate at 1s granularity? We want to see micro dips.
[04:02] Luis: Yep, we'll push that metric to the bench spreadsheet.
[04:05] Maya: Quick check — any blockers from your infra side Derek?
[04:08] Derek: Need to confirm dev cluster can run the extra nodepool; should be fine but I will confirm by EOD.
[04:12] Karen: And what about fallbacks? If the aggressive profile misbehaves, what's the rollback plan?
[04:16] Luis: We have canary based rollout and automatic fallback policy; runtime will detect p99 degradation beyond threshold and revert to previous profile. We'll also set a manual kill-switch in the ingress layer.
[04:26] Priya: One more thing — costs of burst capacity. Maya, you mentioned an addendum?
[04:29] Maya: Yes, I'll send a pilot pricing addendum that outlines burst pricing and a daily cap option.
[04:33] Karen: Great. Also, can you include a simple runbook for our on-call engineers so they know which metric to watch?
[04:38] Maya: Will do.
[04:41] Luis: Action recap: 24h steady-state with aggressive continuous_batching on nodepool A, concurrency cap for chat at 16, prefix TTL up, metrics at 1s granularity.
[04:50] Derek: We'll also try a small ingress soft-throttle to smooth immediate bursts.
[04:54] Maya: Perfect. Any other issues?
[04:56] Karen: Nothing else from me.
[04:58] Priya: All good.
[05:00] Maya: Ok, we'll reconvene after the steady-state run. I'll send the follow-up calendar invite for the bench review and the pricing doc. Thanks everyone.

Note: transcription has minor mislabels and a few words garbled (e.g., "kay-vee cache" for KV cache, "aggressive continuous" sometimes truncated).
notes: Links referenced during call: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/s/bench-nimblex), pilot runbook (link: https://redwood.app/r/runbook-pilot). Maya to attach pricing addendum in follow-up email.
